name: The FDA Real Time Clinical Trials Pilot
blurb: The FDA's move to review trial data as it arrives, and its AI pilot.
title: The FDA Real Time Clinical Trials Pilot
answer: In 2026 the FDA announced steps toward real time clinical trials, in which the agency sees trial data continuously rather than at the end, starting with sponsors including AstraZeneca and Amgen. It also sought input on an AI enabled optimization pilot for early phase studies, covering uses such as modelling and dose selection.

reading.body:
In 2026 the FDA moved toward reviewing trial data continuously rather than at the end, and opened an AI optimization pilot for early phase studies.

The two changes are separate but point the same direction. Real time review means the agency sees data as it arrives, which only works if the data arriving is already clean and validated. The AI pilot, covering modelling and dose selection in early phase studies, is the narrower piece: it is a request for input, not an approved method.

For AI specifically, the constraint is upstream of the models. Continuous review turns data cleaning from a back office task into a condition of participation, and sponsors named as starting points, AstraZeneca and Amgen, carry that burden first. The pilot's stated uses, modelling and dose selection, sit early in a trial where fewer patients and faster decisions matter most.

What this does not establish is scope or timing. The data gives no start date for either effort, no completion date, no list of pilot participants, and no detail on what the FDA will accept as evidence from an AI derived model. It also says nothing about the compute or infrastructure behind continuous data pipelines, so any claim about what those pipelines cost to run is outside what is known here.

sections.body: Sponsors joining real time review need clean, continuously validated data pipelines; AI that cleans data as it arrives becomes a prerequisite.
